h: When the Beach Day Turns Into a Battle
p: Bournemouth has miles of sandy beach running from Southbourne round to Sandbanks, and on a sunny day it's tough to drag anyone off it. But the British seaside has a habit of switching moods quickly, and when the clouds roll in, the town centre is where everyone ends up. That's when an indoor games bar becomes the hero of the holiday.

It's a handy spot for groups staying in town. Bournemouth's station is on the edge of the centre, and from there it's a walk or quick bus ride to the seafront and the main shopping streets. Lots of visitors stay in the hotels around the East and West Cliff, so getting back after a night out is usually just a short stroll.

For hen and stag weekends, a games bar is a really useful first-night plan. It gets everyone talking, it doesn't depend on the weather, and it gives you a bit of structure before the night carries on. Think about booking an earlier slot if you're planning to head into the clubs later, and agree a few prizes and forfeits in advance to keep things lively.

If you've got time to explore beyond the town, Boscombe Pier and its seafront are just along the coast, and Hengistbury Head offers big views over Christchurch Harbour. Further afield, the Sandbanks chain ferry crosses to the Purbeck side, where Studland's beaches and the start of the Jurassic Coast make a fantastic day trip. Come back for the games, and you've got the perfect seaside combo.
